text.title: Retrieval Cost Ledger — Output Contract
text.summary: The artefact this methodology produces: a Retrieval Cost Ledger as YAML or JSON, machine-checkable by the bundled validator, and the required input to `context-graph-engineering`.

contract.field: What is being retrieved over, in one line.
The incumbent structure being measured. Not the one being proposed.
ISO date of measurement. A ledger without a date cannot be compared to anything (r6).
Model and tokenizer used. Both sides of any comparison must match (r6).
How the queries were drawn from real traffic (r2).

The ledger rows. Each item: `id`, `text`, `shape` (`fact`|`multi_hop`), `index_tokens`, `candidate_tokens`, `body_tokens`, `correct` (bool), optional `synthetic` (bool, excluded from derived numbers).
Median of (index + candidate + body) across non-synthetic rows (r5).
The p90 value, plus `p90_query_id` naming the row (r4).
Which query produced the p90 figure, so the tail is inspectable.
Median of ((index + candidate) / body) per row, to one decimal. The verdict number (r5).
Sum of all tokens over all non-synthetic rows divided by the count of `correct: true` rows. Punishes cheap retrieval that fails.
One-off construction cost. `0` for flat retrieval with no build step (r6).
How often the build cost is repaid — e.g. `per merge to main`, `weekly`, `never`. Amortisation input for r6.
The routing outcome from 06-decision-tree.xml, recorded so the ledger is actionable rather than informational.

section.title: Derived numbers are recomputed, not asserted
section.statement: The validator recomputes `median_tokens_per_lookup`, `p90_tokens_per_lookup`, `overhead_ratio` and `tokens_per_correct_answer` from the rows and rejects the ledger on mismatch. A ledger is a table of measurements plus arithmetic; a stated summary that disagrees with its own rows is the most common form of retrieval-cost fiction.

section.title: Consistency rules the validator enforces
section.statement: At least ten non-synthetic rows. Every row carries all four measurement fields and they are non-negative integers; `body_tokens` MUST be greater than zero — a row that delivered nothing is a retrieval failure, not a cost measurement, and belongs in the eval harness. At least one row has `shape: fact` and at least one has `shape: multi_hop` (r2). `p90_query_id` resolves to a real row id. `verdict` MUST be consistent with `overhead_ratio`: a ratio at or above 5.0 cannot record `leave_alone`.

section.title: Handoff
section.statement: `median_tokens_per_lookup` is the value that fills `cost_incumbent_tokens` in a Graph Design Record. A ledger that stops before that field is complete, but the downstream gate in `context-graph-engineering` will refuse it.
